predecessors.name: Kamakura shogunate
predecessors.text: the whole Kamakura realm, taken over by Go-Daigo's imperial government after the siege of Kamakura on 18 May 1333

successors.name: Ashikaga shogunate
successors.text: the realm Takauji took over: the infobox 'Succeeded by: Ashikaga shogunate, Northern Court and Southern Court'

successors.name: Southern Court
successors.text: the mountains of Yoshino, where Go-Daigo set up the Southern Court after leaving Kyoto in January 1337

ledger.x: 1333: Go-Daigo's Kenmu Restoration begins at Kyoto.
1333: the Kamakura realm passes to the restored imperial government.
1335: the Ashikaga break with the court.
1336: Takauji enters the capital and the Kenmu Restoration ends.
1336: the Kenmu Restoration ends with Takauji's entry into Kyoto.

wars.name: Genkō War
wars.outcome: Go-Daigo's side won: the Hōjō garrison at Rokuhara was destroyed in 1333 and Kamakura fell on 18 May 1333, ending the shogunate.

wars.name: Ashikaga Takauji's rebellion against the Kenmu government
wars.outcome: Takauji entered the capital on 25 February 1336 and the Kenmu Restoration ended; the Ashikaga shogunate was established on 11 August 1336 and Go-Daigo withdrew to Yoshino in January 1337.

certainty.note: A three-year regime with no surveyed frontier; the outline is the Kamakura realm Cliopatria carries over, and rule outside the capital region was contested.
